The '''1905 German football championship''' was the third time clubs in Germany competed for the national title under the auspices of the [[German Football Association]] (DFB). There were eleven entries into the competition, marking a new record. For the first time, the holders were given an automatic spot in the competition, taken by [[VfB Leipzig]] who had won the [[1903 German football championship]] and had reached the final in the year before, when the competition was annulled.<ref name=weltfussballfinal>{{cite web|title=Deutsche Meisterschaft 1904/1905 .:. Finale|url=http://www.weltfussball.de/spielbericht/deutsche-meisterschaft-1905-finale-union-92-berlin-karlsruher-fv/|work=weltfussball.de|accessdate=27 July 2011}}</ref>

The large number of participants and the differences in strength persuaded the DFB to hold preliminary rounds before the quarterfinals. However, the dire financial situation of [[SV Blitz Breslau|Schlesien Breslau]] and [[1. FC Lokomotive Leipzig|VfB Leipzig]] led to those two teams not travelling to their matches.<ref name=weltfussballprel2>{{cite web|title=Deutsche Meisterschaft 1904/1905 .:. Qual. 2. Runde|url=http://www.weltfussball.de/spielplan/deutsche-meisterschaft-1905-qual-2-runde/0/|work=weltfussball.de|accessdate=27 July 2011}}</ref><ref name=weltfussballquarter1>{{cite web|title=Deutsche Meisterschaft 1904/1905 .:. Viertelfinale|url=http://www.weltfussball.de/spielplan/deutsche-meisterschaft-1905-viertelfinale/0/|work=weltfussball.de|accessdate=27 July 2011}}</ref>  New matches were scheduled, making for a confusing schedule and semifinals with only three teams.

Both finalists appeared for the first time with [[Blau-Weiß 1890 Berlin|Union 92 Berlin]] winning their only national title.
